newsitem.title: USA: U.S. aluminum orders sharply up Jan-May - Spector.
newsitem.headline: U.S. aluminum orders sharply up Jan-May - Spector.

text.p: U.S. aluminum mill product daily orders rose 16.8 percent in January to May on a seasonally adjusted basis compared to the same period last year, industry analyst Stewart Spector said.
Last month the daily order rate was up 17.4 percent from May 1996, Spector said.
"However, end users are still working with their suppliers on the basis of just-in-time delivery, and continue to run with skinny inventory levels," Spector said.

"Rather than hold extra stocks, in many instances consumers are often willing to pay a premium to get the unanticipated metal units they might need to meet their own production schedules," Spector added.
Non-can sheet bookings were up 16.8 percent in May above the same month last year, January through May were up 23.1 percent.
Can sheet orders in May were up 19.3 percent from the same month last year, but up just 0.7 percent in January through May.
However, Spector said it the orders were adjusted for downgauging of canstock, they would be up some 3 percent.
